scope: synthetic CPU countermodels; NOT an actual12B experiment

causal_mechanisms.reuse: prefix site stores u=f(x); first/explicit-share/duplicate read u
causal_mechanisms.recompute: prefix site stores raw x; each query re-executes f(x), never reading a cached u

conclusion: A natural donor changes f(x) and x together. Both mechanisms pass the explicit-sharing witness, show excess transfer for duplicate versus independent coincidental computations, and match the same-value control.
injective_donor_issue: For fixed reverse/not, same-result different-input donors do not exist. Noninjective functions permit these donors but do not distinguish the two mechanisms here.

same_input_different_table_repair.countermodel: Site stores the donor function table, not its evaluated result. Each query recomputes f(x); x probes remain unchanged.
same_input_different_table_repair.conclusion: Fixing raw x and probing x does not rule out copying the changed operator/table. No abstract computation-reuse identification from these observables.

limitation: Not a universal impossibility theorem: other interventions or observables might distinguish mechanisms. The present proposal does not specify them.

readout_extension.scope: The original enumeration checked answer values only. This explicit common head shows a possible equal-logit extension, not empirical equality of actual model logits.
readout_extension.example: Both countermodels pass explicit sharing and show this positive duplicate-versus-independent margin difference; the recomputation model never reads a stored result.
readout_extension.code_permutation: Equal vectors remain equal after any common permutation of the four response codes.

novelty: Protocol counterexample, not a novel structural identity or a paper contribution.
